TI Countercurrent multiplication revisited: key conceptual updates and
   framework expansion
SO ADVANCES IN PHYSIOLOGY EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE countercurrent multiplication; equilibrium; NKCC2; quasi-stationary
   state; renal osmoregulation
ID CONCENTRATING MECHANISM; DIURETICS; UREA
AB Building on my 2023 paper (Kuang SY. Adv Physiol Educ 47: 665-671, 2023), this article revisits countercurrent multiplication (CCM) and makes three advances. First, it presents an enlarged, detailed, classroom-ready diagram that illustrates how the corticopapillary osmotic gradient (OG(ISF)) emerges, and it further refines the previously proposed concept of the Na+-K+-2Cl(-) cotransporter (NKCC2) activity gradient (AG(NKCC2)) along the thick ascending limb (TAL) into the NKCC2 transport rate gradient (RG(NKCC2)), a more inclusive formulation for explaining the formation of the OG(ISF). Second, it reinterprets Delta OC, the transepithelial osmotic difference across the TAL, as an emergent, system-level outcome produced collectively by many TALs and amplified cycle by cycle during CCM. Third, it expands the earlier CCM-equilibrium renal osmoregulation framework by reconceptualizing renal osmoregulation as a highly dynamic and adaptive regulatory system. In this framework, renal osmoregulation operates within a continuously regulated regime punctuated by episodic CCM activation. CCM represents an intrinsic regulatory mechanism that may be activated intermittently to produce transient, steplike increases in urine-concentrating ability when the prevailing regulatory regime alone cannot meet osmoregulatory demand for maintaining body fluid balance. This reframing offers a physiologically plausible account of how renal osmoregulation operates over time. Together, these advances may provide a clearer, classroom-friendly picture of renal osmoregulation and suggest testable ideas for future research.

TI Discovering Crosscutting Concepts in Science Through Free Play: A
   12-Week, Two-Cohort Study of Elementary Students
SO EDUCATION SCIENCES

   concepts (CCC)

AB This experimental study investigates the interrelationships among personality traits, academic integrity, and group work learning, aiming to identify factors associated with dishonest behaviour in group work learning through a social constructivist lens. TI Encountering the Sacred Past: Religious Experience and Historical
   Empathy in Assassin's Creed Valhalla
SO EDUCATION SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE historical empathy; historical video games; <italic>Assassins Creed
   Valhalla</italic>; history learning
ID VIDEO GAMES
AB Historical empathy is a key concept in history and social studies education. It involves understanding how people in the past thought, acted, and experienced the world through engagement with historical context, perspective taking, and affective connections to historical actors. While these competencies are often developed through written sources and historical narratives, visual and interactive media may offer additional opportunities for fostering historical empathy. This article examines whether the historical video game Assassin's Creed Valhalla may provide affordances for historical empathy for players. Set in Viking Age England and Norway, the game's representations of Norse and Christian religion form the focus of the analysis. The study combines systematic gameplay analysis with qualitative thematic analysis. The empirical material was analyzed for historical empathy and compared with historical sources. The findings suggest that the game may provide opportunities to support historical empathy by helping players understand how people in the past interpreted and navigated the world through religious and cultural frameworks. However, historical simplifications and gameplay-oriented adaptations may limit this potential unless accompanied by teacher scaffolding and critical reflection. Thus, while Assassins Creed Valhalla may be engaging and pedagogically valuable, it should be approached critically as an entertainment product rather than a straightforward representation of the past.

AB Due to the intersection of factors such as cultural practices, socioeconomic context and living conditions, not only the educational experiences and outcomes, but also the environmental attitudes of Roma students are potentially different from those of non-Roma students; this suggests that the commonly implemented environmental education programs and recycling awareness campaigns may not be as effective as previously assumed. Yet, empirical research focusing on Roma students' environmental behavior remains scarce; the aim of this study is to examine the environmental attitudes and recycling behavior of Roma students to inform the existing environmental education approaches and to detect the areas that require attention. Results based on quantitative data showed that most students (57.9%) did not recycle, while the availability of recycling infrastructure emerged as a decisive factor for the respondents who reported recycling. Irrespective of their recycling engagement, most students perceived that environmental protection contributes to quality of life and acknowledged the negative impact of waste on human health. Moreover, categorical regression analysis showed that recycling engagement was associated with parents' occupation and the place of residence. Finally, despite the socioeconomic challenges, the findings indicate an overall positive attitude towards environmental protection, challenging widespread stereotypical assumptions about this ethnic group.

TI How ESD-Relevant Is Teacher Training? An Empirical In-Depth Analysis of
   In-Service Teacher Training Courses in Germany
SO EDUCATION SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE Education for Sustainable Development; ESD; in-service teacher training;
   teacher professional development; educational monitoring; education for
   sustainability
ID PROFESSIONAL-DEVELOPMENT
AB Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) is widely regarded as a key task for schools, yet its implementation depends strongly on teachers' opportunities to develop ESD-related professional expertise. This study examines how ESD is represented in state-accredited in-service teacher training (TT) in Germany, focusing on the degree of ESD relevance and selected characteristics of ESD-related TTs, including duration, school-type specificity, participation numbers, and cancellation. The analysis is based on 1186 ESD-related TT course descriptions from six German federal states, collected for the school year 2022/23 and the first half of 2023/24. The findings highlight the need to consider ESD-related TT offers from a differentiated perspective and to complement the present document-based analyses with additional data to better capture contextual needs and conditions.

TI Effects of Simulation-Assisted Electronics Instruction on Eighth-Grade
   Students' Achievement in Croatian Primary Education
SO EDUCATION SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE simulation-assisted instruction; electronics education; student
   achievement; Tinkercad Circuits; teacher-guided simulation; practical
   activities; eighth-grade students; quasi-experimental research
ID VIRTUAL LABORATORIES; COMPUTER-SIMULATIONS; COGNITIVE LOAD; SCIENCE
AB Electronics education is challenging because students must coordinate abstract electrical concepts, circuit representations, physical components, measurements, and observable circuit behavior. This study examined whether teacher-guided simulation integrated with hands-on electronics work was associated with higher achievement. A matched-class quasi-experimental design included 205 Croatian eighth-grade students aged 14-15 years from five primary schools, with one experimental and one control class in each school. Both conditions used the same curriculum content, worksheets, physical components, measuring instruments, and teacher guidance; the experimental condition additionally used teacher-guided Tinkercad Circuits simulation. TI Measurement Invariance and Validity of Mathematics Self-Concept Scale in
   TIMSS 2023: Evidence from Hong Kong
SO EDUCATION SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE mathematics self-concept; measurement invariance; TIMSS 2023; validity
   evidence; psychometrics
ID FIT INDEXES; ACHIEVEMENT
AB The present study examined the factor structure, measurement invariance across sex and language, concurrent and discriminant validity and achievement-related criterion validity of the eight-item mathematics self-concept scale from TIMSS 2023 in a sample of 4463 eighth-grade students in Hong Kong. Cronbach's alpha was high (alpha = 0.86) and a confirmatory factor model accounting for wording-related method variance fit the data substantially better than a strictly unidimensional model. Findings support the mathematics self-concept scale's practical utility for describing students' perceived mathematical competence and for making cross-group comparisons while cautioning against overreliance on a strict unidimensional structure that ignores negative wording effects. Implications, limitations and future directions of the present study are discussed.

TI An Educational Perspective on a Conceptual Framework for Fuzzy Thinking
   in Early Childhood: Picture Books as Artistic Mediators
SO EDUCATION SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE fuzzy thinking; fuzzy sets; fuzzy logic; early childhood mathematics;
   picture books; mathematics and art; graduality
AB Grouping, classification, and logical reasoning activities in early childhood education have traditionally been grounded in classical set theory and binary logic. Fuzzy set theory and fuzzy logic extend this framework by allowing degrees of membership and truth values between the two binary extremes, giving rise to fuzzy thinking. Recent studies indicate that children as young as four years old already show early manifestations of this type of thinking. However, empirical research has largely focused on graduality, while the broader conceptual principles underlying fuzzy thinking in early childhood remain insufficiently articulated. This article revisits and extends a previously developed conceptual framework, leading to three main contributions. First, it proposes the framework's principles as potential learning goals for the conceptual development of fuzzy thinking. Second, it introduces picture books as artistic mediators of these principles through narrative and visual representations. Third, it presents Will I Eat a Frog Today? as a picture book deliberately designed to mediate the first two principles through narrative and illustration. Overall, the article reconceptualizes fuzzy thinking in early childhood in terms of conceptual development rather than mathematical formalization, providing a foundation for future research and educational resource design.

LA English
DT Article
DE fiberoptic bronchoscopy; anesthesiologists; virtual reality; health

   medical education
AB Background: Fiberoptic bronchoscopy training is constrained by high equipment costs and limited patient availability. This pilot feasibility and usability study describes the development and preliminary evaluation of a Simulation-Based VR Bronchoscopy Training system that incorporates game-design elements (an objective-based task, real-time scoring, and feedback) within an ADDIE-driven development framework. A high-fidelity prototype was built for the Meta Quest 3. Methods: Ten experienced anesthesiologists completed a pre-test, a one-week practice period (participants were instructed to complete at least 3-4 sessions/week, approximately 4-6 h total, with standardized technical support), and a post-test. Perceived realism was rated highly (21.90/25.00) and motion sickness was minimal (2.80/30.00). Conclusions: This pilot study indicates that the simulation is feasible, usable, and well accepted by experienced anesthesiologists, with a preliminary improvement in simulated procedural fluency. Given the small, experienced, single-group sample and the absence of a control condition, these findings should be interpreted as evidence of feasibility and usability rather than demonstrated training effectiveness; larger, controlled studies including novice learners are needed.

TI The impact of GeoGebra®-based dynamic visualization on the mastery of
   circle theorems among senior high school students
SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE circle theorems; dynamic visualization; mathematics education;
   non-parametric statistics; sign test; GeoGebra (R)
ID GEOGEBRA
AB Students often experience difficulty mastering Circle Theorems because conventional instruction relies on static diagrams that provide limited opportunities to visualize geometric relationships. This study investigated the impact of GeoGebra (R)-based dynamic visualization on Senior High School (SHS) students' mastery of Circle Theorems using an explanatory mixed-methods quasi-experimental design. Fifty-eight students participated, comprising an experimental group (n = 22) taught with GeoGebra (R) and a control group (n = 36) receiving conventional instruction. Interview findings indicated that dynamic visualization enhanced conceptual understanding, mathematical reasoning, problem-solving, and engagement, despite initial technological challenges. The findings suggest that GeoGebra (R)-based dynamic visualization can support the teaching and learning of Circle Theorems and should be integrated strategically into mathematics instruction alongside appropriate teacher preparation.

   satisfaction; executive functions; higher education; user perception;
   user satisfaction
ID INFORMATION-SYSTEMS SUCCESS
AB Digital assessment of executive functions in higher education presents opportunities to analyze cognitive performance, user experience, and system usability within scalable academic settings. This dataset includes task-level records from 64 undergraduate students who completed six web-based cognitive tasks, user satisfaction ratings from 55 participants via a 15-item Spanish End-User Computing Satisfaction survey, and thematic annotations of open-ended feedback. All data underwent standardized preprocessing to ensure row-level consistency, variable harmonization, and de-identification. This resource facilitates reproducible research on digital cognitive assessment, user satisfaction benchmarking, task design, and exploratory links between performance and system perception in academic environments, supporting secondary analysis and the evaluation of emerging digital assessment frameworks.

TI A research training ecosystem model (RTEM) to guide development of
   effective research training programs
SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Bronfenbrenner's Ecological Systems Theory; Comprehensive Researcher
   Development Framework; program development; program evaluation; research
   training; research trainee
ID ENVIRONMENT; IMPACT
AB Research training is a long, complicated, and idiosyncratic process, impacted by the nature of each research project, individual trainee characteristics, and factors in the research training environment. Consequently, designing effective research training programs is challenging. To address this challenge, we adapted Bronfenbrenner's Ecological Systems Theory to create a Research Training Ecosystem Model (RTEM) that incorporates factors that impact research trainee growth and development as identified in the published literature. Research training program directors can use the RTEM to identify and map their unique research training ecosystem, then use their map to develop and iteratively revise learning opportunities in their program that leverage the positive impacts and mitigate the negative impacts of individual characteristics and environmental factors.

TI Greater than the sum: programs to support the whole student in STEM
   during and after college
SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE cohort program; Louis Stokes Alliance for Minority Participation
   (LSAMP); post-college impact; program evaluation; STEM; STEM retention
ID SENSE
AB Broadening participation in STEM remains a critical challenge for higher education. This study examines the "Focusing on Cultivating Scientists" (FOCUS) program at Carleton College, a curriculum-based cohort initiative designed to support students from historically excluded backgrounds through a "whole student" pedagogical framework centered on three pillars: drive to succeed, support for learning, and a sense of belonging. A decade of longitudinal evaluation data, including multi-year surveys, qualitative interviews, and institutional student records, revealed significant impacts on student persistence and areas for improvement. Findings demonstrate that while FOCUS students enter college with high STEM interest, they face significantly more obstacles than their peers. These results underscore the conceptual importance of integrating academic support with intentional community-building and near-peer mentorship, and suggest that evaluation feedback cycles can help programs reach these outcomes.

TI Teaching at the right level with digital tools: a large-scale
   quantitative study of learning gains and implementation factors
SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE digital education; educational technology; effect size; learning gains;
   TARL
ID ONE LAPTOP; METAANALYSIS; INSTRUCTION; TECHNOLOGY
AB Teaching at the Right Level (TARL) has shown considerable promise in developing countries, but we still lack solid quantitative evidence about how it works when combined with digital tools. This study evaluates the effectiveness of digitally enhanced TARL and identifies implementation factors associated with the best outcomes across different subjects and grade levels. We used a pre-post design with 1,152 students spanning 8 grade levels and 3 subjects (Arabic, French, Mathematics), assessing students with a 3-level classification system and conducting multiple statistical analyses, with non-parametric tests (Wilcoxon signed-rank, Kruskal-Wallis, Spearman correlation) treated as the primary basis for inference given the ordinal nature of the outcome measure, and parametric equivalents reported as a robustness check. The results were striking: TARL demonstrated significant effectiveness with a Cohen's d of 1.279 (p < 0.001) and 75.2% of students showing positive learning gains. Fourth-grade primary students achieved particularly exceptional results with a mean gain of +1.472 and 50% reaching excellence level. Daily digital tool usage proved crucial (+1.011 vs. +0.604 for non-usage), and the combination of videos, audio, and educational platforms was the combination most strongly associated with maximum learning gains. Surprisingly, we found that lower student autonomy actually correlated with better outcomes (r = -0.614, p < 0.001), suggesting that intensive adult supervision was associated with better outcomes than independent learning in this sample. Our findings indicate that TARL with digital tools was associated with exceptional effectiveness, under the conditions tested, when implemented with daily usage, targeted grade-level focus, and intensive teacher supervision, with the fourth-grade model providing a practical framework that other programs may wish to pilot and evaluate.

ID PERFORMANCE; STUDENTS; ANATOMY
AB Introduction Collaborative learning is widely used in STEM education, but its effectiveness is often challenged in heterogeneous classrooms where students differ in prior knowledge, technical experience, and readiness for participation. This study developed and examined a readiness-informed design framework for stabilizing collaborative learning through structured grouping, role-based accountability, and checkpoint-supported feedback.Methods A design-based implementation study with mixed-methods evaluation was conducted in a biomedical engineering Modern Microscopy course. TI Artificial intelligence-supported learning and higher-order cognitive
   outcomes: the mediating role of metacognitive self-regulation
SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE AI task scaffolding; artificial intelligence in education; cognitive
   offloading; critical thinking; metacognitive self-regulation;
   problem-solving
AB The growing adoption of AI in higher learning institutions poses important questions regarding its effects on higher-order cognitive competencies of students. Although previous studies have investigated perceptions of learning influenced by AI, very little information exists regarding the cognitive processes involved in AI interactions influencing learning performance. The present study sought to establish the relationship between AI task scaffolding, AI verification literacy, and cognitive offloading tendency in terms of their impacts on critical thinking and technical problem-solving of learners, with metacognitive self-regulation as the mediating factor. A cross-sectional design was employed using data from 533 university students across Ghana. Structural equation modeling (SEM) with bias-corrected bootstrapping in AMOS (version 23) was used to estimate the hypothesized relationships. The results indicate that AI task scaffolding is positively associated with both critical thinking and technical problem-solving, whereas cognitive offloading tendency is negatively associated with these outcomes. AI verification literacy does not directly predict the dependent variables but exerts indirect effects through metacognitive self-regulation. These results suggest that the educational value associated with AI-supported learning depends on how students engage with AI systems. The study contributes to the literature by shifting attention from AI adoption to AI interaction mechanisms and highlighting metacognitive self-regulation as the key pathway linking AI-supported learning to higher-order cognitive outcomes.

AB Introduction Video is a common medium used to deliver learning content in Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs). Research on video in MOOCs has mainly explored usage from a learning analytics perspective, focusing on learner viewing patterns, different pedagogical video styles, and learner engagement. A few studies in the literature have proposed video design principles. Still, these focus on enhancing standalone videos rather than providing a framework that explains and guides their role within the broader pedagogical context of MOOCs.Methods A practice-based interpretive research design with a mixed-methods approach was applied to analyze the design work of video-making in a MOOC that explored how teachers can integrate digital technologies into their classroom practices. The analysis focused on the design work involved in producing and positioning videos within the overall course structure. Learner engagement with the videos was also analyzed using aggregated video completion-rate data from two course runs.Results The study proposes six video design principles for practitioners to use in the video-making process in MOOCs and how these can be aligned and positioned with a MOOC platform's pedagogical orientation.Discussion Although effort was invested in designing and producing the videos, the completion-rate data did not show consistently high learner engagement. The finding indicates a contradiction between intended learning design and learners' actual video use, indicating that learners can be more selective in how they use videos in MOOCs.

TI When confidence misleads: misconception categories in three-tier
   diagnostic assessment through a mathematical resilience lens
SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE confidence-understanding misalignment; diagnostic assessment;
   mathematical resilience; mathematical resilience interpretation (MRI);
   misconception; three-tier diagnostic test
ID STUDENTS MISCONCEPTIONS
AB Three-tier diagnostic tests use confidence ratings to distinguish genuine misconceptions from knowledge gaps; however, they rarely interrogate what that confidence represents-a blind spot that is magnified in mathematics-anxious and rote-oriented classrooms. This study proposes Mathematical Resilience Interpretation (MRI), an exploratory lens that employs mathematical resilience profiles to reinterpret confidence-related diagnostic categories and examine the affective patterns associated with students' diagnostic responses. Unlike conventional three-tier approaches that primarily use confidence as a classification criterion, MRI treats confidence-understanding misalignment as an interpretive phenomenon and examines it alongside students' mathematical resilience profiles. Using an embedded mixed-methods design, we administered a three-tier diagnostic test on polynomial factorization to 52 Grade ten students in a Thai secondary school, alongside the Mathematical Resilience Scale (MRS) and structured and unstructured interviews. Students were categorized by their predominant diagnostic response patterns, and descriptive statistics were used to analyze MRS scores across aspects. Replacing the multiple-choice second tier with open-ended reasoning was designed to reduce option-based guessing and revealed a distinct "lack of confidence" category, in which students reasoned correctly despite selecting "not sure". Interpreted through MRI, a discernible pattern emerged: relatively high scores on the value and struggle aspects but persistently low scores on the growth aspect, particularly among students exhibiting confident misconceptions and those who underestimated the correctness of their work. MRI provides an exploratory means of distinguishing patterns of demonstrated understanding from confidence misalignment and highlights growth-oriented beliefs as a potentially relevant dimension for further investigation. These findings may help teachers distinguish students who demonstrate low confidence despite correct reasoning from those exhibiting confident misconception patterns, thereby informing more differentiated pedagogical responses. Theoretically, MRI offers a preliminary interpretive framework for examining how diagnostic response patterns may be understood in relation to students' confidence-understanding alignment and mathematical resilience profiles.

TI Smart Notes for interdisciplinary learning
SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE connective thinking; undergraduate education; interdisciplinary
   learning; liberal arts and sciences; note taking; smart notes
ID NOTE-TAKING; STUDENTS
AB Introduction In this article we show how we implemented the method of Smart Note for Bachelor students in the Liberal Arts and Sciences programme at Utrecht University (LAS). LAS students follow a flexible, interdisciplinary curriculum where they encounter knowledge from diverse disciplinary courses. By using the slip-box technique-separate, concept-focused notes linked together-students can build a personal knowledge map with the help of the digital tool Obsidian. This approach encourages active processing of insights and the explicit connection of disciplinary perspectives.Methods We employed an educational design-research cycle. First, a survey of 81 LAS students (44 final-year, 6 second-year, 31 first-year) and interviews with 7 students were conducted to capture existing note-taking habits. Based on these insights, we designed and refined two pilots within the core interdisciplinary courses at LAS and created an e-learning, consisting of knowledge clips and linked assignments. Student ambassadors co-created the e-learning and supported students during the pilots.Results Students organize notes in varied ways-most chronologically or by chapter, while a minority create custom structures. Because note-taking is highly personal, the intervention emphasized flexibility in how Smart Notes are produced. Although many students internally connect disciplinary ideas, only a few already use digital tools such as Obsidian; those who do report that the tool helps with connecting insights. Pilots showed that scaffolded activities, aligned with course learning objectives, facilitated Smart-Note creation. However, differences in digital literacy limited the uptake of Obsidian, and office-hour attendance was low despite ambassador promotion.Discussion LAS students show the motivation and epistemic fluency required for taking Smart Notes, yet this requires a shift from their habitual linear note-taking practices. Flexible tools and structured activities support them in making Smart Notes, thereby fostering connective thinking. The findings underline the importance of offering tool-agnostic flexibility while embedding clear scaffolds within core courses. Ongoing evaluation of the first-year core-course implementation and further research on teacher support needs are recommended. Student ambassadors proved vital for peer modelling and for demonstrating the value of non-linear note-taking in an interdisciplinary context.

TI Evaluating autism support programs in higher education through the
   perspectives of students, parents, counselors and staff
SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE autism support programs; education accessibility; higher education;
   post-secondary transition; young adults
ID COLLEGE-STUDENTS
AB Introduction Some postsecondary institutions have established Autism Support Programs (ASP) that provide specialized support for autistic college students.Methods This work investigates the structure and experience of these programs through thirty-four semi-structured interviews with participants from four stakeholder groups: ASP staff, autistic college students, parents of autistic college students, and high school staff who have worked with college-bound autistic students.Results Participants reported ASPs offering an array of academic, social and environmental support. AB The purpose of this study was to determine whether using Critical Plurilingual AI Literacy as pedagogy changes Algerian University students' perceptions and providing sociolinguistic agency (the ability to consciously direct AI to operate using an entire repertoire of languages; as well as subverting the AI's norm of only utilizing a monolingual way of working with data). TI Teachers' visual gaze behavior toward children during teacher-child
   interaction in early childhood education and care
SO LEARNING CULTURE AND SOCIAL INTERACTION
LA English
DT Article
DE Visual gaze behavior; Teacher-child interaction; ECEC teacher;
   Eye-tracking
ID JOINT ATTENTION; PLAY; INFANT; CLASSROOM; ENGAGEMENT; QUALITY; PEERS
AB Teachers' visual gaze is central to pedagogical interaction, yet little is known about how early childhood education and care (ECEC) teachers allocate visual attention to children during teacher-child interaction. This study explored ECEC teachers' (N = 4) gaze behavior in groups of children under three years of age. Four teachers wore mobile eye tracking glasses during pedagogical activities, including teacher-led activities and play activities. Eye tracking data were analyzed with epistemic network analysis using teacher-and child-initiated interactions as units of analysis. The results from this study suggest that teachers' gaze patterns differed by activity context: in teacher-led activities, teachers' visual gaze was directed mainly to several children's faces, whereas during play activities it was more often directed to the face and other body areas (body/legs/hands/arms) of the child who was most actively engaged in the focal interaction at that moment. Gaze behavior did not differ clearly between teacher-and child-initiated interactions. Overall, these findings provide initial evidence that ECEC teachers' visual gaze behavior may adapt to the interaction context. These results can inform ECEC teachers' reflection on situational visual attention during interactions with toddlers.

TI Community-based sport for autistic children and young adults: A scoping
   review of inclusion models, program characteristics, and reported
   outcomes
SO RESEARCH IN AUTISM
LA English
DT Article
DE Autism Spectrum Disorder; Adapted Physical Activity; Community sport;
   Inclusion; Public health priority
ID PHYSICAL-ACTIVITY; SPECTRUM DISORDERS; SEDENTARY BEHAVIORS; AQUATIC
   SKILLS; BARRIERS; ADOLESCENTS; EXERCISE; OBESITY
AB Background: Autistic children face barriers to community sport participation despite known benefits. This scoping review, including stakeholder input, examined community-based sport programs, focusing on inclusion models, characteristics, and outcomes. Methods: Following Joanna Briggs Institute and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, four databases were searched. Two reviewers screened and extracted data. Findings were synthesized descriptively and thematically and interpreted alongside input from a stakeholder focus group. Results: Thirty-eight studies (n = 938; mean age = 10.8 years; 78% male) were included, mainly involving children with mild to moderate autism. Aquatic, combat, and team sports were most frequent. Programs typically involved structured similar to 56-minute sessions, once or twice weekly over similar to 12 weeks, with intensive staffing-usually no more than two children per adult. Most programs comprised only autistic children, while mixed groups of autistic and non-autistic children were less common. Benefits mainly concerned motor and social outcomes. Stakeholders also highlighted emotional regulation, autonomy, and family well-being. Inclusion depended more on adapting activities to participants' needs than on sport type. Conclusion: Despite a limited and heterogeneous evidence base, appropriately adapted and supported community sport may offer meaningful opportunities for autistic children's participation, development, and well-being. Sustained participation alongside non-autistic peers remains insufficiently studied. More inclusive provision will require context-sensitive adaptations and coordinated support for community clubs, including staff training, access to autism expertise, and adequate staffing. Community sport should therefore be further investigated as a potentially valuable component of public health strategies supporting autistic children and their families.

TI "Untangle the knot": Maternal blame, emotional reciprocity, and pathways
   toward autonomy in mothers' narratives of autistic young adult sons
SO RESEARCH IN AUTISM
LA English
DT Article
DE Autistic young adults; Mothering; Mother-son relationships; Masculinity;
   Maternal blame; Emotional reciprocity; Autonomy
ID SPECTRUM DISORDER; CHILDREN; PARENTS
AB Background: As autistic young adults transition to adulthood, family support often remains important. Yet mothers' continued involvement can be interpreted as overprotection rather than being understood in relation to ongoing support needs and uneven institutional responses. Although research has documented the demands of maternal caregiving, less is known about how mothers experience continued caregiving and emotional reciprocity as their autistic children move toward adulthood and how they envision their children's futures. This study examines these experiences among Taiwanese mothers of autistic young adult sons. Methods: This study reports a focused analysis of in-depth interviews with 13 Taiwanese mothers of autistic young adult sons enrolled in higher education. Conclusions: Situated in Taiwan, the findings challenge assumptions that continued maternal involvement necessarily reflects overprotection or is incompatible with autonomy. Mothers' narratives instead offer a relational understanding of developing autonomy as shaped by care and the social conditions surrounding autistic young adults.

TI Numerosity perception and fraction processing in children with
   developmental coordination disorder: Dissociating numerical acuity from
   inhibitory control
SO RESEARCH IN DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITIES
LA English
DT Article
DE Developmental coordination disorder; Numerical cognition; Fraction
   magnitude processing; Executive Functions
ID APPROXIMATE NUMBER SYSTEM; RATIONAL NUMBERS; COMPARISON STRATEGIES;
   EXECUTIVE FUNCTIONS; MOTOR COORDINATION; DIFFICULTIES; KNOWLEDGE
AB Children with Developmental Coordination Disorder (DCD) often struggle with mathematics. However, the cognitive factors associated with these difficulties are still poorly understood. In particular, it is unclear whether mathematical problems in children with DCD reflect deficits in executive functions or in more domain-specific numerical processes. The present study examined these associations using two tasks that tap into numerical processes and inhibitory executive functions at different levels of mathematical complexity. In the numerosity comparison task, participants compared two arrays of dots and judge which is more numerous. Performance on this task reflects numerical acuity but also inhibition, which is required to suppress task-irrelevant perceptual information such as the size or spacing of dots. In the fraction comparison task, participants compare the magnitudes of two fractions, a task that requires fraction magnitude processing but also inhibiting the natural number reasoning. Participants were 60 children aged between 10 and 14 years, including children with a formal diagnosis of DCD and age-matched typical developing (TD) controls. In the numerosity comparison task, children with DCD showed less precise numerical acuity than TD peers, but were not more susceptible than TD to interference from task-irrelevant cues. In contrast, in the fraction comparison task, children with DCD showed stronger interference from the Natural Number Bias (NNB), suggesting greater difficulty inhibiting earlier acquired natural number principles. Overall, these findings highlight the multidimensional nature of the mathematical difficulties faced by children with DCD and shows that the problems may have different origins, possibly depending on the age of acquisition.

TI Surface enactment of competency-based curriculum reform: Evidence from
   geography classrooms in Vietnam
SO TEACHING AND TEACHER EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Competency-based curriculum (CBC); Curriculum implementation; Geography
   education; Vietnam; Policy-practice gap
ID POLICY IMPLEMENTATION; KNOWLEDGE
AB Despite the global adoption of competency-based curriculum (CBC), a persistent gap exists between policy intentions and classroom practice. Empirical studies on CBC enactment are scarce, especially in geography education and Asian contexts. This study examines CBC enactment in Vietnamese geography classrooms through video analysis of 24 secondary-level lessons, integrating three frameworks: Curriculum Genre Theory, LUKAS competence-oriented task framework, and foundational CBC principles. The findings reveal a recurring pattern of surface enactment across the lessons analyzed, in which visible reform features coexist with unchanged core pedagogical structures. Across all analyzed dimensions, examination-oriented constraints steer instructional practice toward knowledge reproduction, contrary to reform objectives. The concept of surface enactment provides a theoretical lens to understand partial implementation as a coherent teacher response to conflicting systemic demands. These results suggest that substantive transformation requires addressing assessment culture alongside instructional practices, with significant implications for CBC implementation in centralized, examdriven educational systems worldwide.

TI Making explicit the distinctive metapedagogy of teacher educators
SO TEACHING AND TEACHER EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Teacher educators; Metapedagogy; Selection; Professional learning
ID EXPERIENCE; KNOWLEDGE; IDENTITY; RESOURCES; CLASSROOM; FRAMEWORK;
   IMPACT; RACE
AB This article addresses the limited scholarly attention given to the specialized expertise of teacher educators. Despite their critical role in supporting preservice teachers, the term "teacher educator" remains overly broad, often inclusive of anyone teaching teachers. To address this, the authors propose a framework that defines the metapedagogy of teacher educators as supporting preservice teachers in integrating theory, experience, and situated understanding to navigate the complex interplay between student learning and identity. The framework identifies three central loci of practice-(re)designing, analyzing, and (re)envisioning-which are essential for both teacher educators' metapedagogy with preservice teachers and their own professional development. By clearly articulating this specialized "second-order" knowledge, the authors aim to improve the selection, preparation, and ongoing professional learning of teacher educators. Through the framework, the authors argue that making the metapedagogy of teacher educators visible is both a scholarly and a political act.

TI Trajectory of teachers' work engagement during and after the COVID-19
   pandemic
SO TEACHING AND TEACHER EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Work engagement; COVID-19; Longitudinal study; Job demands-resources
   model; Trust relationship
ID JOB-SATISFACTION; LEADERSHIP; BURNOUT; CONSEQUENCES; INSECURITY;
   EMPLOYMENT; MODEL
AB This five-year longitudinal study examined trajectories of Japanese teachers' work engagement during and after the COVID-19 pandemic (FY2020 - FY2024). Drawing on the Job Demands-Resources model, it analysed 10,922 teacher-year observations from high school and special needs school teachers, using three-level generalised linear mixed models (years nested within teachers nested within schools), with within-between decomposition. Engagement remained stable through FY2021, declined sharply in FY2022 and showed no meaningful recovery by FY2024, indicating sustained post-pandemic deterioration. Trust relationships with students, colleagues and principals predicted individual engagement; student and principal trust reflected the same trend at the school level. The protective role of principal trust intensified over time. Schools with low collective principal trust exhibited progressive disengagement, whereas high-trust schools remained stable. Within-teacher increases in overtime were consistently associated with lower engagement. The findings suggest that the post-pandemic period constitutes a distinct organisational phase requiring sustained leadership investment and engagement monitoring.

TI Effects of varying time constraints on quality, linguistic features, and
   fluency behaviors in L2 writing
SO ASSESSING WRITING
LA English
DT Article
DE Fluency; Time constraints; Writing assessment
ID SYNTACTIC COMPLEXITY; 2ND-LANGUAGE; WRITERS; LIMITS
AB Although previous research has explored how L2 writers allocate their time and how time limits influence writing scores, many of these studies focus solely on final texts, providing only a partial understanding of the writing process. A more comprehensive investigation is essential for enhancing the construct validity of writing assessments. Drawing on empirical research on timed writing and on theoretical models of the writing process, this study explores how time constraints affect L2 learners' written texts and fluency behaviors. A total of 123 participants (60 highintermediate and 63 advanced EFL learners) completed an argumentative writing task with keystroke logging software under either a 30-minute or 60-minute condition, and stimulated recalls were conducted with a subset. The texts were analyzed for syntactic and lexical complexity, fluency, and overall quality. Results indicate that time constraints did not significantly affect linguistic complexity or writing quality, although fluency behaviors differed across conditions. Time constraints thus affected learners' writing processes more than the linguistic quality of their texts. The core implication for L2 writing assessment is that, for test takers experienced with timed writing, shortening the time allotted to an argumentative task changes composing processes without compromising the product-based scores on which assessment decisions rest.

TI Generative AI in computing education: A systematic review and a
   framework for responsible integration
SO COMPUTERS AND EDUCATION: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE
LA English
DT Article
DE Academic integrity; Assessment redesign; Computing education; Generative
   AI; Human-AI interaction in education; Large language models;
   Over-reliance; Programming education; Snowballing; Systematic literature
   review
AB Context. Since late 2022, the rapid uptake of generative AI (GenAI) tools such as GitHub Copilot and ChatGPT has outpaced computing educators' evidence base for responding to it. Objective. This systematic literature review synthesises empirical evidence on four interconnected dimensions of GenAI in computing and programming education: effects on learning outcomes, student over-reliance, assessment integrity, and pedagogical adaptation. Method. Following Kitchenham and Charters (2007) guidelines and Wohlin's (2014) snowballing from seven curated seed papers, screening yielded 72 primary studies (2022-2026) from 33 venues, each was quality-assessed on a 10-item checklist (mean 8.32/10). Thematic synthesis (Cruzes and Dyba, 2011) produced 14 themes. Results. Short-term efficiency gains are robustly replicated (36 studies) but are offset by a comprehension-completion trade-off: AI-assisted completion does not transfer to independent skill (21 studies) and is moderated by prior knowledge (6 studies). Passive over-reliance is widely documented (21 studies), with guardrail tools, self-regulated-learning scaffolding, and scaffold withdrawal as promising interventions (20 studies). Most standard assessments are AI-completable (13 studies), undisclosed AI use is widespread (45-65%; 13 studies), and AI-resistant assessment design is the most densely evidenced theme (26 studies). Conclusions. Responsible integration requires coordinated action across all four dimensions. We derive the VIE Framework (Verification, Implementation, and Equity): three interdependent design requirements, and treat ing any one in isolation underperforms. Seven priority research gaps are identified, notably the absence of longitudinal skill-development and cross-national equity studies.

TI Characterization of patient communication skills through virtual reality
   in physiotherapy students
SO EDUCACION MEDICA
LA Spanish
DT Article
DE Health communication; Physical therapy education; Simulation-based
   education; Virtual reality; Educational assessment
AB Introduction: Communication is a key clinical competency in health professions education; however, the early identification of areas for improvement in communication during undergraduate training remains heterogeneous. Virtual reality (VR) may offer standardized environments for observing communication skills. Objective: To characterize physiotherapy students' patient communication skills through a simulated clinical interview in virtual reality (VR) and explore its usefulness for identifying areas for improvement in communication. Methods: This study used an action research design within the Scholarship of Teaching and Learning (SoTL) framework and was conducted during the second semester of 2025 in the Clinical Semiology course. Each student completed an individual simulated clinical interview in VR using a communication skills training software. Automated descriptive metrics and narrative feedback were collected from the reports generated by the software. The unit of analysis was each valid report/interaction. Descriptive statistics and a descriptive thematic synthesis guided by the Calgary-Cambridge framework were applied. Results: Thirty-five valid reports/interactions were analyzed. Mean duration was 9.6 +/- 1.9 min, and the automated global score was 6.6 +/- 0.8. The descriptive thematic synthesis identified strengths in greeting, respectful interaction, listening, and initial open-ended questions, as well as areas for improvement in framing, discourse organization, adaptation of technical language, and interview closure. Conclusion: VR may complement the characterization of patient communication skills and help identify areas for improvement, providing input for teaching and curricular decisions in health professions education.

TI Indigenous K-12 Students' Access to STEM in Canada: Barriers and
   Promising Practices
SO CANADIAN JOURNAL OF SCIENCE MATHEMATICS AND TECHNOLOGY EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Indigenous education; K-12; Canada; Culturally responsive pedagogy;
   STEM; Two-Eyed Seeing
AB This thematic literature review examines barriers and promising practices shaping Indigenous K-12 students' participation in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education across Canada. Seventeen sources published between 2014 and 2024 were analysed using a combined deductive and inductive coding approach. The review identifies eight key challenges, including systemic inequities, linguistic and identity marginalization, epistemic injustice, and digital access gaps, alongside six promising practices such as land-based learning, culturally responsive pedagogy, mentorship, and knowledge-bridging frameworks, including Two-Eyed Seeing. Findings indicate that Indigenous students' experiences in STEM are shaped by historical, policy, and resource conditions, as well as classroom practices. Engagement is more likely when learning is grounded in local knowledge systems, relational approaches, and Indigenous-defined success indicators. The study highlights the need for sustained policy investment, teacher preparation in Indigenous pedagogies, and culturally grounded evaluation frameworks. It contributes a Canadian synthesis that integrates systemic analysis with practice-level insights, offering direction for educators, policymakers, and researchers seeking to design equitable and culturally relevant STEM education that aligns with reconciliation and Indigenous self-determination.

TI Challenges and Recommendations in Preparing Secondary School Teachers
   for STEAM Education: Comparative Lessons from Austria and Spain
SO CANADIAN JOURNAL OF SCIENCE MATHEMATICS AND TECHNOLOGY EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE STEAM education; Teacher education; Secondary school teachers; Teacher
   professional development
AB Despite the global popularity of science, technology, engineering, arts, and mathematics (STEAM) education, implementing this transdisciplinary approach remains highly demanding. A key challenge is preparing teachers for STEAM instruction, as current teacher education and professional development programmes often remain rooted in monodisciplinary structures. This study explores the challenges and recommendations for preparing secondary school teachers in STEAM education based on the experiences of teacher educators in Austria and Spain. Using a qualitative descriptive phenomenological approach, ten teacher educators were interviewed, and the data were analysed thematically. Findings reveal that Austrian secondary school teachers face time constraints and reluctance to extend classroom time, while Spanish secondary school teachers struggle with rigid, government-mandated curriculum. Austrian teacher educators recommend practical teaching resources, whereas Spanish teacher educators emphasise project replication and forming STEAM communities of practice. Teacher educators in both countries advocate for cross-disciplinary collaboration. The study highlights the need for context-responsive training and systemic support, including flexible curricula and collaborative professional environments.

TI Electrophysiological Evidence for Map-Based Perspective Taking and
   Wayfinding Efficiency in Taiwanese Gifted and General Students
SO GIFTED CHILD QUARTERLY
LA English
DT Article
DE IQ; mixed methods; spatial giftedness; spatial perspective taking;
   gifted students; spatial cognition; wayfinding
ID COGNITIVE CONTROL; MENTAL ROTATION; INDIVIDUAL-DIFFERENCES; INTEGRATIVE
   THEORY; REFERENCE FRAMES; DELTA-RESPONSES; SPATIAL ABILITY;
   RATING-SCALES; KNOWLEDGE; MODELS
AB Spatial perspective taking (SPT) is a fundamental cognitive ability and a predictor of achievement in STEM fields. Gifted students often excel in spatial tasks, yet the neural mechanisms underlying this advantage remain insufficiently understood. This study investigated behavioral and electrophysiological correlates of SPT in Taiwanese gifted versus general high school students using a novel map-based self-localization paradigm that required aligning egocentric (street-view) and allocentric (map-view) perspectives under different location conditions with varying angular disparities (south [0 degrees], east [90 degrees], west [90 degrees], north [180 degrees]). Behaviorally, both groups found the north (180 degrees) condition most difficult, as reflected in lower accuracy and slower responses. Nevertheless, gifted students maintained higher accuracy and shorter reaction times across different location conditions, including east (90 degrees), west (90 degrees), and north (180 degrees). Electrophysiologically, gifted students demonstrated larger N200 and P300 amplitudes at parietal-occipital (POz) and frontal (Fz) electrode sites, reflecting enhanced conflict control and perspective shifting. No group differences were observed at the central site (Cz), indicating that neural advantages were localized to fronto-parietal networks. Time-frequency analyses further revealed stronger delta oscillations in gifted students, suggesting more efficient large-scale synchronization and integration of spatial information. These findings align with mental model theory and support the neural efficiency hypothesis, offering new insights into individual differences in navigation skills. The results underscore the importance of spatial perspective taking for real-world wayfinding and suggest potential training interventions to improve map-use abilities across populations.

TI Academic Inbreeding and Collaboration Patterns: A Comparative
   Publication Profile of Two Turkish Universities
SO HIGHER EDUCATION QUARTERLY
LA English
DT Article
DE academic inbreeding; academic mobility; AVES & Idot;S; higher education;
   international collaboration; scientific collaboration; T & uuml;rkiye
ID SCIENTIFIC PRODUCTIVITY; INFORMATION EXCHANGE; IMPACT
AB This study examines how academic inbreeding relates to scientific collaboration through a publication-level comparison of two Turkish universities during 2018-2022: Hacettepe University, a long-established, research-intensive public university and TED University, a young foundation university. Using AVES & Idot;S publication records (N = 6292) and staff profiles (N = 1371), authors are classified into two mobility profiles, distinguishing those with international degree or work experience from those whose education and employment are entirely domestic. A publication-level inbreeding category is then assigned according to whether author teams comprise only one profile or combine both. Collaboration is measured across six co-authorship settings, and internationally co-authored publications are further classified by the World Bank income group of partner countries. Findings reveal a marked institutional contrast. At Hacettepe, domestic collaborations are predominantly produced by teams composed entirely of authors with domestic-only education and work experience. Such teams also account for a substantial share of internationally co-authored publications. At TED, internationally co-authored publications more often involve teams composed entirely of authors with international experience. These results suggest that internationalisation can coexist with institutionally reproduced networks shaped by mobility, internal reproduction and network openness.

TI A typology for inclusive mathematics education practices
SO SUPPORT FOR LEARNING
LA English
DT Article
DE inclusive mathematics; inclusive practice; Special Educational Needs;
   typology
ID LEARNING-DISABILITIES; STUDENTS; INSTRUCTION; STRATEGIES; TEACHERS;
   PEDAGOGY
AB This paper examines Inclusive Mathematics Education (IME) practices for students with Special Educational Needs (SEN) in upper primary and lower post-primary settings. In response to the absence of shared conceptualisations of SEN and IME, the study adopts a conceptual research design and develops a typology grounded in analysis of existing literature. The aim was to categorise dominant forms of IME practice and to examine the SEN and inclusion contexts within which these practices are positioned. The analysis identified three principal approaches to SEN: General SEN, Specific SEN and Unidentified SEN. Two perspectives on inclusion were also identified, defined as Broad and Narrow. Across the reviewed studies, four dominant types of IME practice emerged: Teaching for Understanding, Constructivist Teaching, Differentiated Instruction and Teaching for Procedural Fluency. Each type comprised associated variants. This typology provides a foundational framework for conceptualising IME practice and highlights areas for further refinement, particularly where practices overlap or are multi-typed.

TI Developing an AI-Assisted Seminar-Based Learning Platform With Embedded
   Librarian Support: Enhancing Information Literacy of Engineering
   Research Teams
SO COMPUTER APPLICATIONS IN ENGINEERING EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE artificial intelligence; collaborative learning; embedded librarianship;
   engineering education; information literacy
AB Engineering research teams face distinct information literacy challenges requiring integration of patents, technical standards, and rapidly evolving documentation beyond traditional academic resources. This study developed an AI-assisted platform integrating automated recommendation systems, embedded librarian support, and seminar-based collaboration to address these multifaceted needs. The system employed natural language processing for query handling, collaborative filtering for personalized discovery, and knowledge graphs linking engineering concepts across disciplines. A quasi-experimental pre-/post-test design with 60 engineering students evaluated platform effectiveness over 8 weeks, using an ACRL-based instrument with verified reliability and content validity (Cronbach's alpha = 0.87). Participants were assigned to experimental and control groups, with the experimental group accessing the integrated platform while controls received traditional library instruction. Results demonstrated substantial improvements across all information literacy dimensions. The experimental group achieved overall score gains of 0.78 points compared to 0.25 for controls, with large effect sizes (Cohen's d = 1.12-1.45). Search skills exhibited the strongest enhancement with 0.87-point increases, while source evaluation improved by 0.83 points. System performance metrics showed recommendation precision of 0.68 and recall of 0.61, representing improvements of 30.8% and 27.1% over traditional keyword-based systems. System usability assessment yielded a mean score of 73.2, exceeding both the control baseline of 62.8 and the acceptable threshold of 68. These findings suggest that integrating AI personalization, expert guidance, and peer collaboration is associated with meaningful gains in discipline-specific information competencies, pending validation beyond this single-site study.

TI Exploring the Development of Children's Learning and Psychological
   Skills in Preschool Education
SO EUROPEAN JOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE children's learning; executive functional training; high-quality
   education; preschool education; psychological skills; social and
   cognitive development
ID QUALITY; TEACHERS; OUTCOMES
AB Preschool education is important for the development of children's cognitive, psychological and social skills. To examine how the physical activity-based learning affects the learning environment and to determine the mediation of cognitive development and psychological skills development on increasing the children's learning foundation in early childhood. An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design is employed involving pre- and post-test intervention. A total of 742 preschool education stakeholders in China were targeted and sampled to obtain quantitative data through the application of pre- and post-structured questionnaires carried out after a 2-week Movement-Based Learning Camp. Semi-structured interviews with 18 purposely selected participants followed and were analysed using thematic analysis as a method to explain and enrich the quantitative results. The findings showed that the learning environment significantly positively mediated children's early childhood learning foundation via the cognitive development (beta = 0.092) and psychological skills development (beta = 0.076) with a significance level of p < 0.001. From the qualitative findings, the following themes emerged as significant for children's holistic development: movement-based learning, emotional safety, peer interaction, learning motivation, critical thinking and school readiness. It introduces and validates an integrated framework that combines sociocultural theory, ecological systems theory and executive function theory to demonstrate the positive impact of physical activity learning on the foundation of children's early learning through improvements in cognition and psychological skills. Pedagogies based on movement create supportive learning environments that facilitate cognitive and psychological development, thereby forming the foundation of early learning.

TI Bridging Parental Investment and Children's Willingness to Communicate
   With AI: A Serial Mediation of Self-Efficacy and Autonomy in AI-Enhanced
   Informal Digital Learning of English
SO EUROPEAN JOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE AI learning self-efficacy; informal digital learning of English;
   learning autonomy; parental investment; willingness to communicate with
   AI
AB In the context of AI-empowered language education, informal digital learning of English has emerged as a key site for fostering young learners' positive psycho-emotional development. However, limited attention has been paid to how family factors shape children's willingness to communicate with AI. This study investigated how parental investment influences upper-primary students' willingness to communicate with AI in an AI-enhanced informal digital learning of English context, focusing on the mediating roles of AI learning self-efficacy and learning autonomy. Grounded in Social Cognitive Theory and Self-Determination Theory, the study surveyed 659 upper-primary students from eight primary schools. Results revealed a serial mediation pathway: parental investment -> self-efficacy -> autonomy -> willingness to communicate with AI. These findings extend parental investment research into AI-enhanced informal digital learning of English contexts and integrate two major motivational frameworks into a unified model of child L2 psycho-emotional functioning.

TI Through the Teachers' Eyes-Primary School Teachers' Perceptions of
   Knowledge to Inform Their Practice
SO EUROPEAN JOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE epistemic belief; primary school teachers; research-practice gap;
   science-practice gap
ID EDUCATION; BELIEFS
AB This qualitative multiple case study examines teachers' perceptions of what knowledge they find useful, with our two cases being academically and non-academically trained early-career primary school teachers. Six teachers were interviewed to explore how different forms of knowledge influence their teaching practices. Findings indicated that while our two cases used a combination of sources to shape their practice, the academically trained teachers made more reference to scientific research. Non-academically trained teachers expressed openness to scientific evidence, but struggled to engage with it due to lack of accessibility, practical challenges, and a tendency to prioritize experiential knowledge. Ultimately, both groups saw value in practical, immediately implementable knowledge that meets the specific needs of their classrooms.

TI Exploring Teachers' Motivation for Sustainable Adoption of Artificial
   Intelligence in L2 Education: A Descriptive Qualitative Inquiry
SO EUROPEAN JOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE artificial intelligence (AI); descriptive qualitative design; EFL
   teachers; focus group; L2 education; motivations and intentions;
   sustainable AI adoption
ID ACCEPTANCE; AI
AB A growing body of research has indicated that using Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies offers different contributions to second/foreign language (L2) education. However, the intentions and motivations behind such adoption have received insufficient attention in the English as a foreign language (EFL) context. To fill the gap, this descriptive qualitative study employed an online focus group interview with 11 Chinese EFL teachers. The results of thematic analysis demonstrated five major themes regarding motivations and intentions for sustainable AI adoption. The teachers argued that they had sustainably used AI for 'enhancing learners' classroom engagement, 'making learning personalised and adaptive for learners, delivering immediate and instant feedback to learners, 'adding innovation and diversity to instruction', and 'staying updated and current with technology'. The findings highlight a need for providing professional development programmes for EFL teachers to raise their AI literacy and notify them of how their intentions mediate their AI-driven practices.

AB Background Schools are important settings for delivering vaccines. TI How Are Pupils With Reading Difficulties Taught? A National Survey of

DT Article
DE literacy; phonics; reading difficulties; reading intervention; reading

ID COMPREHENSION; ACHIEVEMENT; INSTRUCTION; STUDENTS; IMPACT; POLICY
AB The research reported in this paper explored how reading provision was implemented for pupils with reading difficulties in primary schools, including the factors that influenced practitioners' instructional approaches. The findings from a questionnaire survey of educators working in diverse primary schools in England are reported. There was evidence of marked variation in reading provision across schools, alongside a strong predominance of phonics-based approaches in both whole-class reading instruction and targeted interventions. These findings highlight a disconnect between research evidence showing effective practices for children with reading difficulties and practices in schools. New approaches are needed to ensure a closer match between evidence from high-quality research and optimal practice and policy.

TI Public health frameworks increase student's ability to propose solutions
   addressing health inequity
SO ADVANCES IN PHYSIOLOGY EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE BIPOC; cardiovascular disease; LGBTQIA2S+; physiology; public health
ID BLOOD-PRESSURE; HYPERTENSION; RISK
AB Sexual and gender minority (SGM) adults, as well as Black, Indigenous, and People of Color (BIPOC), face inequities regarding cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk in the United States compared to their heterosexual and White counterparts. We previously found that prehealth students experience low baseline knowledge concerning CVD risks among historically marginalized communities and struggle to propose interventional strategies that could reasonably address these disparities. We hypothesize that incorporating public health approaches that address behavior change (e.g., the health belief model) into a pathophysiology lecture enhances students' ability to problem solve regarding health disparity in SGM and BIPOC communities. A single lecture intervention was delivered to 100 students enrolled in a cardiovascular pathophysiology course. Paired pre- and postintervention surveys evaluating both subjective and objective learning outcomes were used to assess the efficacy of our intervention. Twenty-nine students answered the prelecture survey, and twelve students answered our postlecture survey. Students' knowledge of the mechanistic factors contributing to CVD disparities in BIPOC and SGM populations, and their ability to create solutions addressing these disparities, increased after the lecture intervention. Furthermore, the addition of public health intervention frameworks moderately improved students' ability to propose novel intervention strategies in a population-specific manner. Teaching interdisciplinary models of intervention to physiology students may represent a novel approach that enhances their ability to generate approaches to reducing CVD risk in marginalized communities.

TI Playing Under Pressure: Lived Meanings, Tensions, and Re-Significations
   in Teachers' Ludic Mediation Through Play and Toys
SO EDUCATION SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE play; ludic mediation; lived experience; teacher education; hermeneutic
   phenomenology; toys
ID KINDERGARTEN TEACHERS; PERSPECTIVES; EDUCATION; CONTEXT; GAME
AB Play and toys are central resources for learning; however, their integration into schooling is typically traversed by curricular, evaluative, disciplinary, and institutional tensions, particularly in resource-limited contexts. This study examined the meanings, tensions, and re-significations that shape the lived experience of in-service teachers, pre-service teacher education students, and university teacher educators when mediating instruction with play and toys. A phenomenological-hermeneutic study was conducted in Imbabura, Ecuador, with 61 participants: 27 undergraduate education students, 26 school teachers, and 8 university faculty members. In-depth phenomenological interviews were administered, and the corpus was organized and analyzed using Atlas.ti to support the interpretive traceability of the process. The phenomenological-hermeneutic interpretation yielded five nuclei of meaning: embodied ludic heritage, material scarcity narrated as a source of invention, playing under pressure as a structural condition of the classroom as lived by participants, transformation of the didactic gaze, and the teacher's symbolic horizon. Within this corpus, pressure emerges not as external to play but as a condition participants describe as constitutive of its school-based practice. The study concludes that, in the situated experience analyzed here, ludic mediation appears as a practice that demands professional judgment, contextual sensitivity, and institutional recognition.

TI Student-Faculty Communication in Higher Education: Approachability,
   Academic Distance, and Student Hesitation
SO EDUCATION SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE student-faculty communication; academic distance; approachability;
   student hesitation; higher education
ID UNIVERSITY
AB Student-faculty communication plays an important role in how students express themselves, seek help, and participate in university life. This study examines undergraduate students' communication experiences with faculty members in relation to approachability, academic distance, and hesitation to communicate. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 30 undergraduate students aged between 18 and 23 from five universities in T & uuml;rkiye, and the data were analyzed within a qualitative descriptive framework. The findings indicate that students often consider whether their questions are necessary or appropriate before contacting faculty members and may postpone communication because of concerns about receiving a negative response, being misunderstood, or appearing inadequate. Overall, student-faculty communication is shaped by perceived academic distance, anticipated faculty responses, communication settings, and students' concerns about evaluation.

TI Investigating Relational Understanding: The Quality of Learners'
   Argumentations
SO EDUCATION SCIENCES
LA English
DT Article
DE argumentation; relational understanding; quantitative content analysis
ID PROOF
AB Tasks related to relational understanding are useful for arguing about basic mathematical structures and relationships, and for encouraging long-term mathematical thinking. It has been determined that learners in primary school have considerable difficulties arguing about these relationships. Based on these findings, a study was conducted in which the written argumentations of tasks targeting relational understanding provided by 72 learners aged ten to thirteen were evaluated. The tasks covered various mathematical topics and were divided into tasks involving pattern continuation, explorative argumentation and persuasive argumentation. Responses were evaluated by an inductive-deductive coding scheme. The results showed that learners can describe the relationships, but often struggle to explain the underlying reasons for their occurrence. In comparison to exploring and describing the relationships, the quality of the persuasive argumentations in particular was low. There were no substantial weaknesses in any specific aspect of the argumentations, such as structure or linguistic precision. Nevertheless, performance differed to some extent between tasks addressing different mathematical content, which may point to argumentation as a more domain-specific than domain-general competence. However, given the limited number of tasks per content area, this interpretation remains tentative and warrants further investigation. The findings provide tentative indications of variation across mathematical content areas, but do not allow firm conclusions about the domain-specificity of argumentation competence. Future research should employ multiple tasks per domain and longitudinal designs to disentangle content-related from task-specific effects and to examine how persuasive argumentation competence develops over time.

This study investigates ESD-related belief patterns among pre-service primary school teachers specialising in Natural and Social Sciences in Germany, addressing both the structural configuration of shared beliefs and how these configurations reflect a fundamental tension between ESD as a political programme and ESD as an independent educational concept. Using Q-methodology, 31 pre-service teachers from nine German universities sorted 31 statements about ESD. Factor analysis identified three structurally distinct, yet partially overlapping, viewpoints: ESD as a Whole-School Task of Fostering Autonomy, ESD as a Critical-Transformative Educational Concept, and ESD as an Individual Teaching Responsibility. The viewpoints share a general-pedagogical belief core centred on autonomy, real-world relevance, and cross-curricular responsibility, while explicitly political-critical dimensions of ESD are absent from this shared core. Across the viewpoints, the political and normative orientation of ESD is related in different ways to educational claims of autonomy, independent judgement, and non-indoctrination. The findings have implications for pre-service teacher education and contribute to closing a methodological gap in ESD belief research by revealing how individual ESD-related beliefs are configured and related within distinct viewpoints.

ID RELIABILITY; EDUCATION; VALIDITY; LEVEL
AB Reflective practice is widely recognized as a cornerstone of teachers' professional development and instructional improvement. However, the lack of culturally adapted and psychometrically validated instruments limits the accurate assessment of reflective practice across different educational contexts. This study aimed to translate, culturally adapt, and psychometrically validate the Survey of Reflective Practice (SRP) for use among Greek primary school teachers, providing the first Greek adaptation of the SRP to undergo preliminary psychometric evaluation. TI Place, identity, and adaptation: conceptual insights from elementary
   science education initiatives in rural Hawai'i, Maine, and Montana
SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE elementary education and teaching; place-based education; professional
   learning; rural; science education
ID FRAMEWORK
AB Rural elementary science education presents a wide array of opportunities to provide connection between classroom learning and lived experiences. While existing curricula support teachers in connecting NGSS-aligned scientific sensemaking to the cultural, ecological, and political dimensions of the communities they serve, few frameworks integrate authentic rural educator perspectives and experiences. These challenges are coupled with a changing energy landscape and a need to prepare teachers for a more sustainable future. Overall, through supporting educator reflection and professional growth, and investing in sustained collaborative learning, teachers can develop the place-pedagogical expertise to help young people in rural areas connect to place, honor who they are and where they come from, and build genuine capacity for the future ahead.

TI Exploratory Evidence on ChatGPT Adoption Among Undergraduate Engineering
   Students in Medellín, Colombia: A 2023 Logistic Regression and a 2025
   Descriptive Pilot
SO TRENDS IN HIGHER EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE generative artificial intelligence; ChatGPT; higher education; learning
   strategies; undergraduate engineering education; logistic regression
ID USER ACCEPTANCE
AB Evidence on generative artificial intelligence adoption remains limited in Latin American engineering education, particularly for undergraduate populations in which paid employment may shape study practices. This exploratory study examined reported ChatGPT (GPT-4o model) use among students enrolled in two undergraduate engineering programs at the Instituto Tecnol & oacute;gico Metropolitano in Medell & iacute;n, Colombia. Technology Acceptance Model and Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology research were used as background literature; their core constructs were not measured or tested. In that pilot, all respondents selected ChatGPT, 93.3% selected Gemini (Gemini 2.5 Flash model), and 53.3% selected Copilot (powered by OpenAI's GPT-4o model); the most frequent activities were writing-related support (63.3%) and both idea generation and concept explanation (60.0% each). The findings provide context-specific, hypothesis-generating evidence and support larger multi-institutional studies that directly measure acceptance constructs, use intensity, verification behavior, and educational outcomes.

TI Designing an AI-integrated role-rotation pedagogical model to support
   competence-related learning in pre-service educational psychologists
SO FRONTIERS IN EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE artificial intelligence; design-based research; educational psychology;
   professional competence; role-rotation learning
AB Introduction The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into higher education has created new opportunities for supporting professional learning. However, AI-supported learning, case-based instruction, collaborative role rotation, and reflective practice are often examined separately. Limited attention has been given to how systematic role rotation can structure pre-service educational psychologists' critical engagement with AI-generated information, particularly in gifted education contexts.Methods This study employed a Design-Based Research approach to develop, implement, and refine an AI-integrated role-rotation pedagogical model. The eight-week intervention involved 62 undergraduate pre-service educational psychologists enrolled in a Pedagogy and Psychology program at a Kazakhstani university.
