TI Promoting Proficiency-Oriented Teaching in U.S. Post-Secondary Chinese
   Programs: Teacher Development and Student Self-Directed Learning
SO CHINESE JOURNAL OF APPLIED LINGUISTICS
LA English
DT Article
DE proficiency-oriented world language teaching; Chinese as a foreign
   language curriculum design; NCSSFL-ACTFL Can-Dos; self-directed language
   learning; higher education world language education
ID COLLABORATIVE DESIGN; LANGUAGE
AB Proficiency underachievement remains a key concern for U.S. college-level World Language (WL) programs and a major factor behind declining student enrollment. However, current recommendations-such as regularly measuring student proficiency with standardized tests and implementing program-wide faculty professional development (PD)-are often impractical due to limited resources and varying levels of faculty readiness. In response, the field of Chinese as a Foreign Language (CFL) has increasingly called for innovative, localized solutions. This study employed the 2017 NCSSFL-ACTFL Can-Do Statements (Can-Dos) in a college CFL program to improve two critical areas influencing proficiency outcomes: ongoing teacher PD and student self-directed learning. Two faculty members with differing expertise (language pedagogy vs. comparative literature and culture) engaged in co-design-style professional learning by collaboratively revising the curriculum using the Can-Do standards, with a focus on articulating program goals and implementing corresponding performance-based assessments (e.g., Integrated Performance Assessments). To support student self-directed learning, 35 chapter-level self-assessment checklists based on the Can-Dos were developed and used across seven courses. Using a convergent mixed-methods design, data were collected through a student survey completed by 60 participants, a faculty interview, and a written faculty questionnaire. Results show significant gains in curriculum design and faculty understanding and use of ACTFL standards, especially regarding assessment. Student responses to the self-assessment tools were positive, citing improved abilities to identify learning gaps, set goals, and reflect on strategies. This exploratory study contributes to the growing shift in postsecondary CFL programs toward articulating standards-based goals, designing performance-based assessments, and advancing teacher PD. It also offers insights for other WL programs seeking sustainable ways to improve proficiency outcomes.

TI Current Trends in Chinese as a Second Language Syntactic Complexity
   Research
SO CHINESE JOURNAL OF APPLIED LINGUISTICS
LA English
DT Article
DE automatic syntactic analysis; Chinese as a second language; second
   language proficiency; syntactic complexity; writing quality
ID LANGUAGE
AB Earlier research on syntactic complexity has predominantly focused on English as a second language. However, recent years have witnessed a growing interest in the syntactic complexity of Chinese as a second language (L2). Against this backdrop, this paper reviews the current state of research on L2 Chinese syntactic complexity. We begin by synthesizing studies on the development and evaluation of syntactic complexity measures specific to Chinese, highlighting key differences from those used for English. We then examine research exploring the relationship between syntactic complexity and L2 Chinese proficiency or production quality, along with the influence of various learner- and task-related factors, such as linguistic background and writing genre, on this relationship. Additionally, we discuss recent advancements in the automatic analysis of syntactic complexity in Chinese. The review concludes by proposing potential directions for future research on L2 Chinese syntactic complexity, in hopes of offering insights and practical implications for researchers and educators in L2 Chinese acquisition and teaching.

   Teaching?
SO CHINESE JOURNAL OF APPLIED LINGUISTICS
LA English
DT Article
DE technology; language teaching; Chinese as a second language
ID L2; COMPLEXITY; FLUENCY
AB This paper explores the transformative role of technology in Chinese second language learning (CSL), bridging the gap between research and teaching implications through an overview of existing research, with added specific insights from the author's own work over two decades focusing on communicative approaches to teaching and learning CSL. It examines three areas where innovative uses of technology impact on Chinese language learning in and out of the classroom: digitally-supported pedagogy for authentic, student-centred learning; theory-driven research using corpora and eye-tracking; and virtual immersion during residence abroad. Findings demonstrate how mobile-assisted learning, flipped classrooms, and corpus-informed instruction have been successful in enhancing communicative competence and learner autonomy. Eye-tracking studies assist teachers in understanding cognitive processes underpinning character recognition and reading fluency; evidence gathered during the COVID-19 pandemic offers nuanced insights into identity, confidence, and conversational proficiency developed during virtual residence abroad. The paper argues for a paradigm shift in CSL, advocating for training in digitally-literate pedagogies reflecting learners' sociocultural realities. It concludes by urging integration of generative AI tools to support personalized learning and interactional competence, positioning technology not as a replacement for real-world engagement but as a catalyst for inclusive, resilient, and plurilingual language education in the global "digiverse."

TI A low-cost metabolic apparatus for student labs: measuring oxygen
   consumption and ventilation in conscious mice
SO ADVANCES IN PHYSIOLOGY EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE conscious mouse; low-cost experiment; oxygen consumption; pharmacology
   demonstration; respiratory monitoring
ID KIDNEY
AB Hands-on experience in measuring core physiological parameters like oxygen consumption (Vo(2)) is essential for deep conceptual understanding, yet the prohibitive cost of commercial systems often excludes such experiments from science curricula. To bridge this gap, we developed and implemented a ready-to-use educational module centered on a simple, low-cost metabolic apparatus. The apparatus, constructed from commercially available components, enables direct measurement of Vo(2) and respiratory parameters in conscious mice by students. Moreover, the apparatus was successfully used to detect and quantify the opposing physiological effects of two classic metabolic-modulating drugs: levothyroxine sodium (increasing Vo(2) and minute ventilation) and chlorpromazine hydrochloride (decreasing Vo(2), respiratory frequency, and ventilation). This module transforms abstract principles of energy metabolism, respiratory control, and pharmacology into an investigable, inquiry-based learning experience. The apparatus features straightforward assembly and operation and is accompanied by a comprehensive instructional manual. These attributes render it particularly well suited for integration into undergraduate and graduate physiology and pharmacology laboratories, thereby broadening access to advanced physiological measurement techniques.

TI Cellular and network mechanisms of spreading depolarization
SO ADVANCES IN PHYSIOLOGY EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE brain injury; cell swelling; ionic homeostasis; migraine; spreading
   depression
ID CEREBRAL-BLOOD-FLOW; GLUTAMATE RELEASE; PERIINFARCT DEPOLARIZATIONS;
   EPILEPTIFORM ACTIVITY; MITOCHONDRIAL SODIUM; RECEPTOR ACTIVATION;
   DEPRESSION; RAT; BRAIN; ISCHEMIA
AB Spreading depolarization (SD) denotes a slowly propagating wave of ionic redistribution resulting in neuronal and glial depolarization, cellular swelling, vascular alterations, and metabolic challenge. Tissue characteristics, including brain region and energy availability, influence both entry into and recovery from SD. Although many paradigms reliably induce SD, a nuanced debate surrounds the fundamental mechanism underlying SD initiation and the primary conductances involved. Emerging mechanistic hypotheses of SD induction share a common theme of disruption in ionic homeostasis, often involving sodium-potassium ATPase insufficiency. The prevalence of SD in traumatic brain injury, stroke, migraine with aura, and seizures underscores the clinical relevance of understanding the physiological basis of SD. This Staying Current article describes the potential mechanisms underlying SD initiation, propagation, recovery, and clinical impact from a mechanistic standpoint.

AB Background Despite the growing importance of Health Systems Science (HSS), many emergency medicine (EM) residency programs lack a formal, comprehensive curriculum for health policy and advocacy.Methods We developed a longitudinal Health Policy and Advocacy curriculum by mapping core components, based off those originally proposed in the New England Journal of Medicine, to ACGME milestones. TI Turning Free-to-Use Generative AI into Flipped-Interaction Intelligent
   Tutors: Exploring Student Engagement and Perceptions of Learning
SO CANADIAN JOURNAL OF SCIENCE MATHEMATICS AND TECHNOLOGY EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE Generative artificial intelligence; Intelligent tutoring systems (ITS);
   Pre-service science teacher education; Subject matter knowledge
ID EDUCATION; SCHOOLS
AB An engaging and cost-effective digital tool for developing subject-matter knowledge (SMK) could mitigate educational inequities in resource-constrained contexts. This case study explores the effectiveness of free generative artificial intelligence (GAI) platforms, prompted to function as a Flipped-Interaction Intelligent Tutoring System (FIITS), to promote science student-teacher SMK learning. Data were collected across a 10-week intervention from 42 third- and fourth-year natural and physical sciences student teachers at two campuses of a South African university. The students engaged with the FIITS in odd-numbered weeks by pasting a provided prompt into a free GAI platform, and with benchmarking interactive electronic worksheets in even-numbered weeks. Affective, behavioural, and cognitive engagement and perceptions of SMK learning were analysed using post-session questionnaires, end-of-module reflections, and group interviews. Both modalities elicited consistently high and comparable engagement levels, but students reported stronger perceptions of SMK development with the FIITS. They valued its personalisation, relevance, and human-like interactivity, although workload pressures and occasional GAI errors somewhat hindered the FIITS's effectiveness. These findings suggest that free GAI platforms, prompted to behave as FIITS, may provide equitable, scalable, and pedagogically effective tools for improving SMK in student-teacher education. Recommendations include scaffolding an initial adjustment phase, incorporating varied levels of challenge, and managing novelty and workload to sustain engagement. This study offers early evidence of the pedagogical potential of free flipped-interaction GAI in science teacher education, particularly in contexts where access to costly educational technologies is limited.

TI Enhancing System Dynamics Education Through Smartphone Sensor-Based
   At-Home Experiments
SO COMPUTER APPLICATIONS IN ENGINEERING EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE at-home experiments; engineering education; experiential learning;
   smartphone sensors; system dynamics
ID DEVICES
AB The widespread use of smartphones among college students, combined with the sophisticated sensors these devices contain, enables their use as portable, low-cost measurement systems when paired with simple physical setups. Such at-home engineering experiments offer an engaging and flexible learning environment that can enhance students' understanding of key engineering concepts. This paper reports on using the smartphone gyroscope sensor to conduct two at-home experiments, namely the oscillation of a compound pendulum and the vibration of a cantilever beam, in a junior-level, lecture-only system dynamics course. The aim was to reinforce students' conceptual understanding and experimental skills in system dynamics, a foundational subject for control systems in mechanical and electrical engineering curricula. All students in the class were provided with a physical system to experiment with. The study was conducted over a 4-year period and involved 350 students. Data analysis of the short pre- and post-quizzes administered in each of the two experiments suggests that the at-home experiments had a positive impact on students' understanding of key concepts. Furthermore, written comments from the students indicated that they valued the learning experience gained from performing these experiments.

TI Seeing Sustainability: Aesthetic Public Pedagogy and the Formation of
   Ecological Citizenship
SO EUROPEAN JOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE aesthetic public pedagogy; civic ecological imagination; ecological
   citizenship education; eco-visual literacy; public pedagogy;
   sustainability education; visual culture
ID CLIMATE-CHANGE; EDUCATION
AB Ecological citizenship education has specified responsibility, agency, justice and participation, but it has not fully explained how citizens are formed through visual culture beyond formal education. This conceptual article develops aesthetic public pedagogy as a specific mode of public pedagogy: the contested process through which publicly circulating visual and sensory forms configure ecological relations and invite audiences into ecological subject positions. Unlike public pedagogy, visual environmental communication, arts-based environmental learning or ecological literacy considered separately, the concept explains how aesthetic encounters can transform perceptibility, attachment, interpretation and future orientation in ways relevant to citizenship. Through purposive theoretical sampling and comparative analysis of ecological citizenship education, public pedagogy, and visual and aesthetic environmental communication, the article derives four analytically distinct but non-linear mechanisms: ecological visibility, affective attachment, critical eco-visual literacy and civic ecological imagination. It specifies conditional propositions for each mechanism and integrates spectacle, consumerisation, exclusion and depoliticisation as endogenous distortive pathways shaped by audience position, power and institutional context. The framework does not assume that exposure to environmental imagery produces citizenship. It identifies when aesthetic encounters are more likely to support witnessing, responsibility, critical judgement and collective agency, and when they are more likely to produce passive spectatorship or consumer citizenship. A final operationalisation shows how the framework can guide the design and evaluation of museums, public art, digital platforms and formal educational activities.

TI Exploring the Roots and Remedies of Students' Academic Hatred and
   Boredom in English Language Education: A Descriptive Qualitative Study
SO EUROPEAN JOURNAL OF EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE academic hatred; boredom; descriptive qualitative design; emotional
   experiences; language education
ID EXPLORATION; PROTOTYPE
AB This study adopted a descriptive qualitative approach to explore the roots and remedies of Chinese EFL students' academic hatred and boredom. To this end, a sample of 43 Chinese EFL students was selected through convenience sampling for in-depth interviews. Thematic analysis indicated that academic hatred stemmed from 'language complexity,' 'instructional monotony,' 'excessive pressure', and 'examinations.' The analysis further revealed that student boredom was primarily rooted in 'lack of diversity', 'task difficulty', 'teacher instruction', and 'boring textbooks'. Concerning the remedies, the findings indicated that academic hatred could be alleviated through 'establishing a supportive learning environment', 'changing learning methods', 'setting realistic goals', 'forming positive mindsets/attitudes', and 'having interpersonal communication in the class'. The findings also revealed that boredom could be mitigated by 'diversifying learning materials and tasks', 'establishing a positive classroom climate', 'encouraging group work', and 'connecting learning to real-world situations'. The findings offer valuable pedagogical implications for addressing and managing negative emotional experiences in second language (L2) education and for fostering more engaging and emotionally supportive learning environments.

TI Increasing the Efficiency of Comparative Judgment for Writing
   Assessment: Warm-Starting Estimation and Selection Using NLP
SO JOURNAL OF EDUCATIONAL MEASUREMENT
LA English
DT Article
ID RELIABILITY
AB Comparative judgment (CJ) is an assessment method in which assessors compare pairs of essays and judge which is of higher quality. While CJ produces valid and reliable results, it often requires many judgments before quality scores become reliable. In this study, we examine whether natural language processing (NLP) can improve the efficiency of CJ by warm-starting the estimation of quality scores and the selection of essay pairs. We predict essay quality by fine-tuning a transformer model and use these predictions to construct informative priors in a Bayesian Bradley-Terry-Luce model. We then introduce three selection rules based on predicted scores and essay embeddings. In this study, we focus on Dutch writing assessments in secondary and higher education in two settings: one-off assessments and recurrent assessments. Warm-start estimation reduced the number of judgments required to reach a reliability of .70 by approximately 40%-68% compared with likelihood-based cold-start estimation and by approximately 24%-64% compared with Bayesian cold-start estimation. To reach a reliability of .90, warm-start estimation yielded smaller reductions of around 15% compared with cold-start estimation. The warm-start selection rules we constructed yielded smaller additional gains. In practice, a reliability of .70 was reached after two to four judgments per essay, and a reliability of .90 after seven to fourteen judgments. Overall, warm-starting CJ substantially reduces assessor workload and improves the practical applicability of CJ as a summative assessment method.

TI Collaborative action research for inclusive teacher professional
   learning in early childhood education
SO JOURNAL OF RESEARCH IN SPECIAL EDUCATIONAL NEEDS
LA English
DT Article
DE early childhood development and education; inclusive education;
   participatory action research; professional learning; professional
   learning communities; teacher agency; teacher professional development
AB Inclusive Early Childhood Development and Education (ECDE) requires teachers with the knowledge, skills, and professional agency to respond effectively to diverse classrooms. Despite policy commitments to inclusive education across Africa, many ECDE teachers experience inadequate preparation, fragmented professional development, and limited institutional support. Collaborative participatory action research (PAR) offers a promising approach to teacher professional learning, yet evidence from African contexts remains limited. This study examined how collaborative PAR influenced inclusive teaching competencies among ECDE teachers participating in a regional professional learning initiative across six countries in Southern and Eastern Africa. A qualitative PAR design involved 35 purposively selected teachers over 12 months. Data from project reports, reflective journals, and focus group discussions were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Findings indicate that collaborative inquiry strengthened teachers' understanding of inclusive education, confidence in adapting pedagogy, professional agency, and culturally responsive teaching grounded in local languages, indigenous knowledge, and community participation. The initiative also stimulated institutional reflection and continuing regional professional relationships. Collaborative PAR can strengthen inclusive teacher professional learning by positioning teachers as contributors to professional knowledge and agents of educational change. Embedding collaborative inquiry within teacher education and continuing professional development may support contextually responsive inclusive practice in resource-constrained settings.

TI Reading Side by Side: A Second-Grade Teacher's Inquiry Into Dyad Partner
   Reading
SO READING TEACHER
LA English
DT Article
ID FLUENCY
AB Fluency is a key component of recent literacy legislation in most US states, and these mandates often require regular assessments to identify at-risk students and monitor growth, including measures of reading fluency. This classroom inquiry examined how dyad partner reading was implemented and its impact on 19 second-grade students' words per minute during 9 weeks of daily 10-min sessions. The partner reading routine produced overall gains in reading rate and revealed patterns in the types of support learners needed to progress. Implementation insights also emerged, including the importance of explicit routine teaching, thoughtful partner formation, responsive adjustments, and attention to partner dynamics. These findings suggest that brief, daily dyad partner reading can be a practical fluency intervention within instructional frameworks and highlight implementation lessons that may help teachers apply the routine effectively.

TI A Reproducible Simulation-Assisted Framework for Teaching Nonlinear
   Pendulum Dynamics in Engineering Education
SO COMPUTER APPLICATIONS IN ENGINEERING EDUCATION
LA English
DT Article
DE computational thinking; engineering education; phase-space
   visualization; simulation-assisted learning; symplectic integration
AB Computer-based simulation is increasingly important in engineering-oriented STEM education, but students often experience mathematical modeling, numerical integration, visualization, and physical interpretation as separate learning activities. This study developed and pilot-evaluated a reproducible simulation-assisted framework for teaching nonlinear pendulum dynamics through one aligned workflow. Its distinctive contribution is the explicit connection of analytical model formulation, dimensionless state-space representation, fixed-step numerical integration, phase-space visualization, Hamiltonian energy diagnostics, and assessment of students' interpretation of the contrast between classical RK4 and symplectic St & ouml;rmer-Verlet integration. The pilot implementation involved 30 undergraduate students who completed four computer-assisted laboratory sessions over 12 academic hours. Learning outcomes were assessed using parallel pre-test and post-test instruments covering six dimensions: governing-equation interpretation, phase-space classification, energy-based reasoning, numerical-integration understanding, comparison of RK4 and symplectic integration, and visualization interpretation. The mean score increased from 48.2% in the pre-test to 73.0% in the post-test, corresponding to a mean paired gain of 24.8 percentage points. The paired effect size was large, with Cohen's d_z = 1.87, and the mean normalized learning gain was moderate, g = 0.489. The strongest gains were observed in phase-space classification and comparison of RK4 with St & ouml;rmer-Verlet integration. These results provide pilot evidence that reproducible simulation, visualization, and energy-aware numerical diagnostics can support short-term computational understanding of nonlinear dynamics. Causal or comparative superiority is not claimed because the study used one cohort, no control group, N = 30, one institution, and an immediate post-test.

TI Home-Based Opportunities and Self-Determination in Youth: When
   Intellectual Disability Shapes the Impact of Context
SO JOURNAL OF APPLIED RESEARCH IN INTELLECTUAL DISABILITIES
LA English
DT Article
DE home context; intellectual disability; opportunities;
   self-determination; youth
ID QUALITY-OF-LIFE; YOUNG-CHILDREN; COGNITIVE DISABILITIES;
   DECISION-MAKING; FAMILY-MEMBERS; STUDENTS; ADULTS; PARENTS;
   PERSPECTIVES; INDIVIDUALS
AB Background Home is a key context to foster self-determination. This study examined whether intellectual disability moderates the relationship between home-based opportunities to engage in self-determined actions and self-determination levels.Method Middle and high school students with and without intellectual disabilities (aged 13-22) completed the AIR-S questionnaire, which evaluates self-determination capacity and opportunities at home. A moderation model was used to examine the relationship between home opportunities and self-determination, as well as the moderating role of intellectual disability.Results A positive association was found between home-based opportunities and self-determination. Although intellectual disability was not a significant direct predictor of self-determination, once opportunities were considered, it significantly moderated this relationship, indicating that the positive association between opportunities at home and self-determination became progressively stronger as levels of intellectual disability increased.Conclusions Home-based opportunities play a critical role in fostering self-determination. Intellectual disability conditions how strongly supportive environments translate into self-determined actions.
